findings.statement: the bulk segment writer ingests at least 1.25x the general writer, seal and partitioning inside the window
findings.detail: bulk 395355 ops/s against general 285031 (bulk vs general: greater 1.387x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 13.1%/4.1%)) on 20000 keys in 1000-record durable batches with the drain inside the window. Loop alone: 0.022s against 0.021s; commit phase 0.013s against 0.012s, seal 0.015s against 0.025s, merge 0.016s against 0.025s. f46 priced the writer's floor at 2.04x the general path on the seal alone (F46.1); this is the built writer, with the block table, checksums and superblock it omitted, on the load the engine is judged by

findings.statement: the seal phase is at least 1.8x faster with the bulk writer
findings.detail: seal phase 0.025s general against 0.014s bulk (general vs bulk: greater 1.722x (p=0.0051, rel_iqr 6.6%/8.8%)), as the engine accounts it. The memtable sort and the chain walk are the same in both arms; what differs is Store's hash table, freelist, pending arena and checkpoint against one forward pass. Merge phase, which writes through the same two writers: 0.025s against 0.016s

findings.statement: bulk segments take at most 0.9x the disk of general ones
findings.detail: 3.6 MB on disk with the bulk writer against 3.9 with the general one (0.932x) for 2.2 MB of records; device bytes 9.9 against 9.6 MB. A bulk segment has no freelist rounding, no reuse log, no redo-log arena and no index slack. Space is immune to drift, so this ratio is a plain median ratio

findings.statement: reads over the loaded store do not differ between the writers
findings.detail: 20000 random point reads after the drain: bulk 4962490/s against general 4858149/s (bulk vs general: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.021, p=0.8102) -- within noise, not a result). Same format, same Blob, same routing; a difference either way would mean the writers pack blocks differently enough to matter

notes: two arms interleaved in one process, fresh store per rep, the f42 load shape (durable per batch, partitioning on). The arms differ only in NextOptions::bulk_writer: general writes every piece through Store::create/append/checkpoint/close, bulk through SegmentWriter. The timed window is the load PLUS the drain (flush: seal, join, partition), the shape the external suite times, because on the loop alone the seal overlaps the commits and most of its cost is hidden (F42.3). load_s is the loop by itself. Device bytes from /proc/self/io over the window; disk bytes are the store's files after close; the read sample runs after the drain, so every key is sealed and routed in both arms
